title: Work IQ: granular MCP policies to restrict platforms, workloads and operations
summary: Hold: the licensing field says entitlement is unpublished, although Microsoft documents consumption-based licensing for the Work IQ API that these controls govern. The roadmap dates and policy navigation are supported; the tool count needs qualification, and the cost-management checklist step has no corresponding controls row.

claims.claim: The documented Work IQ MCP tenant policy blocks mutation operations by default, including create, update, delete and actions such as sending email.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.claim: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP exposes ten generic tools.
claims.quote: The Work IQ MCP collapses hundreds of operations into just 10 generic tools
claims.fix: Replace 'through ten generic tools that work on resource paths' with 'through generic tools that work on resource paths'. The cited overview says 10, but https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/mcp/overview lists twelve tool names across its tool categories.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP's generic tools operate on resource paths.
claims.quote: Tools work with relative resource paths. The path shows the resource, and the tool acts as the verb

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Policy cannot grant access beyond the signed-in user's existing access, and policy approval does not bypass the user's permission check.
claims.quote: If policy allows an MCP tool request, the underlying resource access is still checked against the signed-in user's Microsoft 365 permissions. The request fails if the user doesn't have access to the requested resource.

claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'consumption'.
